questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Yesterday my sister go to the market.
Yesterday my sister goes to the market.
Yesterday my sister went to the market.
Yesterday my sister going to the market.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' signals a finished past action, so use the past simple of 'go', which is 'went'.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'very old; from a long time ago'?
questions.explanation: 'Ancient' describes something that is very old, such as an ancient city.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: You can to swim very well.
questions.explanation: After the modal 'can', use the base verb with no 'to' and no -s: 'You can swim'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'My new bag is ______ than my old one.'
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -y change y to i and add -er: 'heavy' becomes 'heavier than'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'The doctor ______ treated me was very kind.'
questions.explanation: Use 'who' to refer to a person: 'the doctor who treated me'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'They ______ already finished their project.'
questions.explanation: Use 'have' with 'they' to form the present perfect: 'They have already finished'.

questions.prompt: Change to the passive: 'A famous artist painted this picture.'
options: This picture painted by a famous artist.
This picture was painted by a famous artist.
This picture is painted by a famous artist yesterday.
This picture were painted by a famous artist.
questions.explanation: Past passive uses 'was/were' + past participle: 'This picture was painted by a famous artist'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'If you heat the water enough, it ______ to boil.'
questions.explanation: The result clause of the first conditional uses 'will' + base verb: 'it will start to boil'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'I have decided. Next year I ______ a small shop. It is my plan.'
questions.explanation: Use 'be going to' for a plan decided before now: 'I am going to open a small shop'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'We sold ______ products today, only three or four.'
questions.explanation: 'Products' is countable and the amount is small, so use 'a few': 'a few products'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'This is the ______ test I have ever taken.'
questions.explanation: Short adjectives ending in -y form the superlative with 'the' + -iest: 'the easiest'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means 'it is forbidden'?
options: You don't have to take photos here.
questions.explanation: 'Mustn't' means an action is forbidden; 'don't have to' would mean it is not necessary.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'a person who is paid to work for someone else'?
questions.explanation: An 'employee' is paid to work for an employer; the 'employer' is the one who pays.

questions.prompt: Combine: 'This is the village. I grew up there.' Best combined sentence:
options: This is the village which I grew up.
This is the village where I grew up.
This is the village who I grew up.
This is the village whose I grew up.
questions.explanation: Use 'where' to refer to a place: 'the village where I grew up'.

questions.prompt: Choose the most natural sentence for a fixed plan with a time.
options: I see the dentist at 4 o'clock tomorrow.
I am seeing the dentist at 4 o'clock tomorrow.
I will seeing the dentist at 4 o'clock tomorrow.
I going to see the dentist at 4 o'clock tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The present continuous is natural for a fixed arrangement with a time: 'I am seeing the dentist at 4 o'clock tomorrow'.

questions.prompt: Read: 'The instructions were so vague that nobody knew what to do.' The word 'vague' means...
questions.explanation: 'Vague' means unclear or not exact, which is why nobody knew what to do.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If the factory closed, hundreds of workers will lose their jobs.
If the factory closed, hundreds of workers would lose their jobs.
If the factory would close, hundreds of workers lose their jobs.
If the factory closes, hundreds of workers would lose their jobs.
questions.explanation: Second conditional: 'If' + past simple, 'would' + base verb, so 'If the factory closed, ... would lose'.

questions.prompt: Report this sentence: She said, 'I am tired.'
options: She said that she is tired.
She said that she was tired.
She said that I am tired.
She said that she were tired.
questions.explanation: In reported speech the tense shifts back: present 'am' becomes past 'was', so 'she was tired'.

questions.prompt: Complete with the correct word form: 'Her ______ to finish the race surprised everyone.'
questions.explanation: After the possessive 'Her' the sentence needs a noun: 'determination'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct passive sentence for: 'They are repairing the bridge.'
questions.explanation: The present continuous passive is 'is/are being + past participle': 'The bridge is being repaired'.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: She is an university student in the capital.
She is a university student in the capital.
She is university student in the capital.
She is the university student in a capital.
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a 'yoo' consonant sound, so it takes 'a', not 'an'.

questions.prompt: Choose the best linking word: 'He studied hard; ______, he passed the exam.'
questions.explanation: Studying hard caused him to pass, so a result linker is needed: 'therefore'.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Each of the students have a book.
Each of the students has a book.
Each of the students having a book.
Each of the students have books each.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'has': 'Each of the students has a book'.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: She enjoys to read in the evening.
She enjoys reading in the evening.
She enjoys read in the evening.
She enjoys reads in the evening.
questions.explanation: The verb 'enjoy' is followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'She enjoys reading'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: 'You haven't seen my keys, ______?'
questions.explanation: A negative statement takes a positive tag using the same auxiliary: 'haven't ... have you'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'The meeting has been postponed ______ Monday.'
questions.explanation: 'Until' shows the point in time up to which something is delayed: 'postponed until Monday'.

questions.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to 'abundant'?
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantities, which matches 'plentiful'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: 'The medicine had a strong ______ on the patient.'
questions.explanation: 'Effect' is the noun meaning result; 'affect' is usually the verb meaning to influence.

questions.prompt: Which word means the opposite of 'visible'?
questions.explanation: The standard negative prefix for 'visible' is 'in-', giving 'invisible'.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with correct and consistent tenses.
options: While she was cooking, the lights go out.
While she was cooking, the lights went out.
While she cooks, the lights went out.
While she was cooking, the lights goes out.
questions.explanation: A shorter past action interrupting a longer one uses the past simple ('went') with the past continuous ('was cooking').

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about the past.
options: If she had studied, she would pass the exam.
If she had studied, she would have passed the exam.
If she studied, she would have passed the exam.
If she would have studied, she had passed the exam.
questions.explanation: The third conditional uses 'If' + past perfect and 'would have' + past participle: 'had studied ... would have passed'.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Despite the heavy rain, the farmers kept working in the fields all day.' What does this tell us about the farmers?
options: They stopped because of the rain.
They continued working in spite of the rain.
There was no rain that day.
They worked for only a short time.
questions.explanation: 'Despite the heavy rain' shows the rain did not stop them; they kept working all day.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: 'After months of planning, the company finally ______ a decision.'
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is 'make a decision', so 'made a decision' is correct.

questions.prompt: Read: 'The new policy was met with mixed reactions: some praised it, while others strongly opposed it.' What does 'mixed reactions' mean here?
options: People reacted in different ways, some positive and some negative.
questions.explanation: 'Mixed reactions' means people responded differently; the text shows both praise and opposition.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that is correctly written (no run-on or fragment).
options: The rain stopped, we went outside to play.
The rain stopped, so we went outside to play.
The rain stopped we went outside to play.
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses must be joined by a comma plus a coordinating conjunction: 'The rain stopped, so we went outside'.

questions.prompt: Read: 'I suppose the food was fine,' she muttered, pushing her plate away. What does her behaviour suggest about how she really felt?
options: She was not really pleased with the food.
She had not tasted the food.
questions.explanation: Muttering and pushing the plate away contradict her words, suggesting she was not actually pleased.
